newsitem.title: JAPAN: JR Tokai applies for Japanese bourse listings.
newsitem.headline: JR Tokai applies for Japanese bourse listings.

text.p: Central Japan Railway Co (JR Tokai) on Monday formally applied for its shares to be listed on four Japanese stock exchanges.
State-owned JR Tokai, aiming to go public in October, has submitted applications for listings on the Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Kyoto bourses.

The planned sales of JR Tokai shares will likely weigh on the Japanese stock market, especially if this were to be followed by further government sales of shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and East Japan Railway Co (JR East), analysts and brokers said.
"Worries about a supply glut are likely to loom in the market early this autumn," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.

"JR Tokai's stock sales would be absorbed by the market, if the Japanese economy starts picking up strongly. But for now, we'll have to carefully watch to see if there will be any impact on the market," Kobayashi said.

JR Tokai, one of six regional railway operators that arose from the break-up of the state-run Japanese National Railways (JNR), which was burdened by mounting deficits, would be the third JR company to be listed on Japan's stock exchanges.
JR East and West Japan Railway Co (JR West) are already traded on Japanese bourses.

Earlier this month, JNR Settlement Corp which is in charge of settling JNR's debt and assets, said it would decide the timing to sell more of JR East shares after shares in JR Tokai have been offered.

In April, a newspaper report said Japan's Finance Ministry planned to sell 500,000 shares of NTT by the end of this year, the first sale of the telecom giant's shares by the ministry in about nine years.

Some brokers said that investors might sell shares of other government-related issues like JR East, JR West and Japan Tobacco Inc to generate profits to buy take part in the auction of JR Tokai shares.
Industry analysts however said their evaluation of JR Tokai shares fell behind that of JR East and JR West.
"Our assessment of JR Tokai is at a discount to JR East and JR West," said Naoto Hashimoto, analyst at Nomura Securities Co Ltd's Financial Research Center.

JR Tokai runs a bullet train service which is used by 100,000 passengers a day, and that currently makes the firm very profitable. But the company's profits are overly dependant on the bullet train service, which is somewhat risky, Nomura's Hashimoto said. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
